title: Private deployments: helm/installer support batching_tier + migration notes + validation steps
creator: Diego Santos
description:
Goal
Ensure Redwood Private (helm charts + private installer) correctly supports the new tiered batching config (batching_tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient), including:
- safe upgrade/migration behavior (no breaking changes; explicit batching overrides still win)
- validation (fail fast on invalid values; clear warnings on ignored fields)
- operator-facing migration notes and a verification checklist for rollout

Context
Runtime-1.21 introduces workload-aware batching defaults via a new tier selector. Hosted/Dedicated can rely on control-plane surfaces; Private must support:
1) chart values + rendered runtime config
2) private installer config schema + migration/validation
3) upgrade notes that explain precedence and rollback

Config changes (Private)
New fields (runtime config layer)
- batching_tier: "fast" | "standard" | "cost_efficient"
- tiered_batching_enabled: boolean (feature flag / kill switch; defaults to false for Private unless set)

Precedence rules (must match runtime)
1) If explicit batching knobs are set, they override tier defaults:
   - max_batch_size
   - max_queue_delay_ms
   - prefill_weight / decode_weight (or equivalent scheduler weights)
   - kv_cache_pressure_limits (if present)
2) If explicit knobs are unset AND tiered_batching_enabled=true, apply tier defaults based on batching_tier.
3) If batching_tier is unset, default to "standard" (but only when tiered_batching_enabled=true).
4) If tiered_batching_enabled=false, ignore batching_tier (but keep it in config for future enablement).

Deliverables
A) Helm chart support
- Add values.yaml support for selecting tier + enabling flag.
- Render into the runtime config ConfigMap / Secret (depending on existing chart pattern) in a way that preserves backward compatibility.
- Add validation at chart-render time where possible (helm schema) and/or runtime startup validation.

B) Private installer support
- Update installer config schema to accept batching_tier + tiered_batching_enabled.
- Migration logic: existing configs continue to work; if explicit knobs exist, do not rewrite them.
- Add preflight validation:
  - reject invalid batching_tier values
  - warn if batching_tier set but tiered_batching_enabled=false
  - warn if explicit knobs present (tier will be ignored)

C) Operator docs / upgrade notes
- Migration guide: what to set, what stays the same, and how to validate.
- Rollback instructions: disable flag; pin prior runtime image; revert chart version.

Implementation notes
Helm values (proposed)
- values.yaml:
  runtime:
    batching:
      tieredBatchingEnabled: false
      batchingTier: standard
      # explicit overrides (existing fields):
      maxBatchSize: null
      maxQueueDelayMs: null

Rendered runtime config (example)
- ConfigMap snippet:
  batching:
    tiered_batching_enabled: {{ .Values.runtime.batching.tieredBatchingEnabled }}
    batching_tier: {{ .Values.runtime.batching.batchingTier | quote }}
    max_batch_size: {{ .Values.runtime.batching.maxBatchSize }}
    max_queue_delay_ms: {{ .Values.runtime.batching.maxQueueDelayMs }}

Validation expectations
- batchingTier must be one of: fast, standard, cost_efficient
- If user sets batchingTier="cost-efficient" (dash) or "eco" -> fail fast with actionable message
- If tieredBatchingEnabled=false and batchingTier set -> warning only (no failure)

Migration guide (operator-facing)
1) Pre-upgrade checks
- Confirm runtime image will be >= 1.21.x.
- Confirm you have a way to roll back chart + image (GitOps tag, Helm release history).

2) Upgrade steps (recommended staged enablement)
- Step 1: Upgrade runtime to 1.21.x with tiered batching disabled (default)
  - tieredBatchingEnabled: false
  - (Optional) set batchingTier: standard to pre-stage the value
- Step 2: Enable on a canary instance / small % of traffic (if you have traffic splitting)
  - tieredBatchingEnabled: true
  - batchingTier: standard
- Step 3: Change tier per route/workload only after validating SLOs (fast tier is streaming-sensitive; cost_efficient increases queueing risk).

3) If you previously tuned batching explicitly
- Keep your existing explicit settings; they continue to override tier defaults.
- If you want to adopt tiers, remove explicit maxBatchSize/maxQueueDelayMs and enable tiered batching.

Verification checklist (post-change)
- Config correctness
  - Use the runtime config explain endpoint (from PR-18470) or equivalent:
    - Confirm effective batching_tier and whether it is active
    - Confirm explicit overrides are applied when present
- Latency / queueing
  - Watch p50/p95/p99 latency for the affected routes
  - Watch queue delay histograms and batch formation stats
  - Watch timeout/cancel rates and load-shed reason codes (especially for cost_efficient)
- GPU utilization
  - Confirm expected utilization increase for cost_efficient tier without violating p95 SLO

Rollback plan
- Immediate mitigation: set tieredBatchingEnabled=false (tier is ignored; runtime returns to previous behavior)
- If needed: revert chart release to previous version + pin runtime image < 1.21 (last known good)
- If explicit overrides were removed, restore them from Git history / your values repo

Links / artifacts
- Helm charts PR: sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr_176.json
- Private installer PR: sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr_98.json
- Runtime config schema PR: sources/github/redwood/pr_18421.json
- Config explain endpoint PR: sources/github/redwood/pr_18470.json

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Helm charts expose tieredBatchingEnabled + batchingTier and pass schema validation.
- [x] Private installer accepts new fields and performs preflight validation + warnings.
- [x] Upgrade notes written (what changed, precedence rules, staged enablement, verification, rollback).
- [x] Basic install/upgrade tested (helm template, kind/minikube smoke, installer dry-run) with:
  - invalid tier -> fails
  - tier set but flag off -> warning
  - explicit knobs + tier -> warning, explicit wins

Risks / notes
- Private customers often run stricter SLOs and have less headroom; do not enable tiered batching by default.
- cost_efficient can increase queue delay and tail latency under bursty loads; operators must validate before enabling broadly.
- Ensure terminology is consistent: cost_efficient (internal) vs “cost-efficient” (docs). Private config must use cost_efficient.
